fields.text: A GLM aquarist writes a 7-line stocking plan from a brief - one species or plant per water zone (surface, two midwater, bottom fish, bottom invertebrates, background plants, foreground plants), each with an exact count - a second GLM turns the plan into a photo brief, and Muse renders the finished tank straight-on through the front glass. Then the loop closes: a Gemini vision checker inventories only what is actually visible, zone by zone with counts, a GLM auditor scores the plan against that inventory - stocked, wrong zone, wrong count, missing, extra - and a Decide judge labels the tank stocked to plan, counts drifted, zones drifted or species missing. The render has to answer to the plan, zone by zone. Four model families, four different jobs. See recipes/aquarium-stocking-audit.md.

nodes.name: Aquarium stocking, zone-checked - plan, render, read back, audit

fields.text: A peaceful freshwater community aquarium in one 60-litre rectangular glass tank, planted and beginner-friendly, colourful, photographed straight-on from the front so the surface, the middle water and the bottom are all visible at once. Hard constraints: only peaceful community fish that stay under 8 cm as adults, no aggressive or fin-nipping species, no goldfish, no fish that uproots or eats plants, schooling fish in groups of at least four, and every plant a real aquatic plant.

fields.system: You are a meticulous aquarium stocker. The input is a brief for one planted freshwater community tank. Write ONE stocking plan in this exact shape: exactly 7 lines, numbered 1 to 7, in this order - line 1 SURFACE fish, line 2 MIDWATER fish, line 3 MIDWATER fish (a different species from line 2), line 4 BOTTOM fish, line 5 BOTTOM invertebrates, line 6 BACKGROUND plants, line 7 FOREGROUND plants. Each line starts with its zone word (SURFACE, MIDWATER, BOTTOM, BACKGROUND or FOREGROUND), then names ONE species or plant type with an exact count and a colour or detail (for example '1. SURFACE: 5 silver hatchetfish, silver with a black stripe'). Fish lines carry an exact count between 4 and 8, the invertebrate line an exact count between 3 and 8, plant lines an exact count of clumps or stems between 2 and 6. Every fish must be a peaceful community species that stays small, every plant a real aquatic plant, and the seven lines must be seven different species or plant types. Honour every hard constraint in the brief. Output the plan only, no preamble, no closing remarks.

nodes.name: Stocking plan - GLM stocks the tank

fields.system: You direct aquarium photography. The input is a numbered 7-line stocking plan: each line names a water zone (SURFACE, MIDWATER, BOTTOM, BACKGROUND plants, FOREGROUND plants), one species or plant type and an exact count. Output ONE image prompt, under 120 words, for a straight-on photograph of the finished tank taken through the front glass: name every one of the 7 lines in plan order with its zone, item, exact count and colour, inside one rectangular glass aquarium that fills the frame, dark gravel substrate, clear water, bright daylight from above, surface line visible at the top, no people, no hands, no text, no labels, no equipment visible, nothing alive in the frame that is not in the plan. Output the prompt only.

fields.question: The text is a 7-line aquarium stocking plan: each line names a water zone (surface, midwater, bottom, background plants, foreground plants), one species or plant with an exact count. The image is a rendered tank that claims to follow exactly that plan. Which verdict fits? 'stocked to plan' means every line is visible in its planned zone at its planned count, with nothing unplanned added. 'counts drifted' means everything is in its planned zone but at least one count is off. 'zones drifted' means every planned species is present at its planned count but at least one is in the wrong zone. 'species missing' means at least one planned species or plant cannot be found anywhere in the tank. Judge the stocking, not the photography.
fields.options:
stocked to plan
counts drifted
zones drifted
species missing

fields.q: You are the tank checker in an aquarium pipeline. Look at this straight-on photograph of a planted aquarium and report ONLY what you can actually see. List what is visible zone by zone in this order - SURFACE, MIDWATER, BOTTOM, BACKGROUND PLANTS, FOREGROUND PLANTS - one item per line, each with the species or plant you see and an exact count. Then list any living thing you can see that does not belong to any of those zones, if any. Do not guess at anything hidden behind a plant or another fish - if you are unsure of an item, give your best guess and mark it '(?)'. Do not compare it to any plan; just report what is visibly there.

nodes.name: Tank check - Gemini reads the tank

fields.system: You are an aquarium auditor. The input gives a numbered stocking plan of 7 lines, each naming a water zone, one species or plant type and an exact count, then the marker 'VISIBLE IN THE TANK:' and an inventory of what a checker could actually see in the rendered tank, zone by zone. Compare the two, line by line. Output one line per planned line, in plan order, starting 'STOCKED - ' if the item is visible in its planned zone at exactly the planned count, 'WRONG ZONE - ' if it is visible at the planned count but in a different zone (name the zone it was seen in), 'WRONG COUNT - ' if it is in the planned zone but the read-back count differs (give the seen count), or 'MISSING - ' if it cannot be found anywhere, followed by the line's short name. Then one 'EXTRA - ' line for each visible fish, invertebrate or plant that is not in the plan, if any. End with one line 'Summary: X of 7 stocked.' Judge by identity, colour, count and zone; a close colour match counts as the same species. Output the audit only, no preamble.
